newsitem.title: INDIA: India zinc down, tin, nickel firm.
newsitem.headline: India zinc down, tin, nickel firm.

text.p: Zinc prices lost gained ground while tin and nickel ruled firm on the local market on Wednesday, dealers said.
Other base metals were steady in limited activity.

Zinc prices fell by 50 rupees at 8,400 rupees per quintal as losses in the world market prompted profit-taking. Zinc was up by 50 rupees on Tuesday. Copper was steady at 13,500 rupees, as was lead at 4,200 rupees per quintal in nominal trade.
Volume was dull as major players awaiting the announcement of selling prices by state-owned agencies for August.
"State-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd. may keep prices unchanged but Hindustan Zinc Limited will hike prices for August," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metals Exchange.
Tin and nickel extended gains on the back of rising international prices. Tin rose by 100 rupees at 29,200 rupees while nickel rose by 200 rupees at 34,300 rupees per quintal.

Aluminium prices moved in a narrow range and finished steady at 7,800 rupees per quintal but the undercurrent was firm as some traders expected local producers to hike selling prices of aluminium shortly, one broker said.
